issues.legal_issue: A tenant’s delivery of possession for repairs or reconstruction does not terminate the existing tenancy, and the tenant’s return is under that tenancy.
material_facts: The tenants delivered possession after orders were made for the landlord to carry out reconstruction.
The landlord had undertaken to offer the premises back to the tenants after the work was completed.
The landlord reconstructed and substantially altered the premises, then offered them to the tenants on new terms.
issues.conclusion: The tenancy did not end when possession was delivered or when the old building was reconstructed. The tenants were entitled to re-enter under the original tenancy and on the terms that applied when they delivered possession, subject to any rent revision permitted by law.
issues.legal_principle: Section 12 distinguishes temporary delivery of possession for repairs or reconstruction from eviction under Section 10: the tenancy continues and the tenant’s right to re-enter survives. Sections 108(b), (c) and (l) of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, address the lessor’s duty to put the lessee in possession, quiet enjoyment, and payment of rent; the doctrine of suspension of rent applies while the landlord possesses the premises. V. Dhanapal Chettiar v. Yesodai Ammal, AIR 1979 SC 1745, explains the continuing protection of a tenancy under rent-control legislation. Kondeti Suryanarayana v. Pinninti Seshagiri Rao, AIR 2000 SC 70, confirms that reconstruction does not defeat the tenant’s right to return. Section headings may assist as general indicators of subject matter but cannot override clear statutory language.

predicates.rent_control_reconstruction_case: The proceeding concerns a tenant’s right to return after possession was delivered under a rent-control process for repairs or reconstruction.
predicates.tenant_delivered_possession_for_reconstr: The tenant delivered possession so the landlord could carry out repairs or reconstruction.
predicates.landlord_undertook_to_offer_premises_bac: The landlord undertook to offer the premises back to the tenant after the work was completed.
predicates.landlord_completed_reconstruction: The landlord completed reconstruction of the premises.

issues.definition: When possession is delivered for reconstruction under a rent-control process and the landlord completes the work after undertaking to offer the premises back, the tenant returns under the original tenancy.

issues.legal_issue: A landlord may seek a lawful rent revision after improvements or reconstruction but may not make payment of an increased rent a condition of the tenant’s return.
material_facts: The landlord substantially reconstructed and altered the premises at the landlord’s expense.
The landlord offered the rebuilt premises at a rent substantially higher than the rent previously paid.
The landlord’s offer made the increased rent a condition of the tenants’ return.
issues.conclusion: The landlord could not insist on the increased rent as a condition of re-entry. The landlord could seek fair-rent revision as permitted by law, and until a lawful revision was made the tenants remained liable at the previous rent.
issues.legal_principle: Section 5(1) of the Andhra Pradesh Buildings (Lease, Rent and Eviction) Control Act, 1960, permits an increase in fair rent where an addition, improvement or alteration is carried out at the landlord’s expense, subject to the statutory limits and the Controller’s jurisdiction to decide disputes. Read with Sections 4, 6 and 12, reconstruction may constitute an addition, improvement or alteration for this purpose. The right to seek revision does not make revision a precondition to the tenant’s re-entry.

predicates.rent_control_reconstruction_case: The proceeding concerns a tenant’s return after possession was delivered for repairs or reconstruction under a rent-control process.
predicates.landlord_made_improvements_at_own_expens: The landlord carried out improvements, additions, alterations or reconstruction at the landlord’s expense.
predicates.landlord_conditioned_tenant_return_on_hi: The landlord required the tenant to accept a higher rent as a condition of returning to the premises.

issues.definition: When a landlord who has made improvements at the landlord’s expense conditions a returning tenant’s access on a higher rent, the landlord may not impose that condition.

issues.legal_issue: A tenant’s application to enforce the landlord’s undertaking to restore possession is not an execution application subject to the execution time limit, but the tenant must seek restoration promptly and within the applicable outer limitation period.
material_facts: The landlord had given an undertaking to offer the rebuilt premises back to the tenants.
The tenants applied to enforce that undertaking after the landlord offered the rebuilt premises on terms they did not accept.
The application was filed more than six months after the relevant appellate orders, and the executing court dismissed it as out of time under the execution rule.
issues.conclusion: The tenants’ application was not an execution application governed by Rule 23’s six-month limit. It was governed by Article 137 of the Limitation Act, 1963, with time running from when the right to apply accrued. The tenant must nevertheless act within the time fixed by the Controller or, if none was fixed, within a reasonable time and promptly upon receiving the landlord’s offer; the three-year period is an outer limit, and delay may defeat relief even within that period.
issues.legal_principle: Rule 23 of the Andhra Pradesh Buildings (Lease, Rent and Eviction) Control Rules, 1961, governs execution applications by a decree-holder, including a landlord seeking to enforce an order requiring the tenant to deliver possession. A tenant enforcing the landlord’s undertaking is not seeking execution of an order in the tenant’s favour, so Article 137 of the Limitation Act, 1963, applies; its period runs from accrual of the right to apply. Mukri Gopalan v. Cheppilat Puthanpurayil Aboobacker, (1995) 5 SCC 5, supports the application of the Limitation Act to an application before a Rent Controller. The contrary Andhra Pradesh High Court decisions in K.S. Hanumantharayappa v. A.N. Vittal Rao, K. Manik Rao v. M. Bikshapamma, and Navin Chandra v. Prema Bai Pitti were overruled.

predicates.tenant_application_to_enforce_return_und: The tenant applied to enforce the landlord’s undertaking to offer the premises back.
predicates.landlord_failed_to_restore_possession: The landlord failed to restore possession in accordance with the undertaking.
predicates.tenant_applied_within_three_years_of_acc: The tenant applied within three years after the right to apply accrued.
predicates.tenant_applied_within_fixed_or_reasonabl: The tenant applied within the time fixed for seeking return or, if no time was fixed, within a reasonable time and promptly after the landlord’s offer.

issues.definition: If a tenant applies to enforce an unfulfilled return undertaking within three years of accrual and within the fixed or reasonable time for seeking return, the application is not barred by the execution time limit.

issues.legal_issue: Current occupants of rebuilt premises must be given notice and an opportunity to be heard before an order restoring possession to the former tenant is implemented against them.
material_facts: The landlord informed the High Court that the rebuilt premises had been leased to other persons.
The record did not establish when or in what circumstances those persons had entered possession.
The Supreme Court left their rights undecided and directed that they be notified and heard before the restoration order was given effect.
issues.conclusion: Before implementing the order restoring possession, the Controller must give notice to the persons then in possession and hear them; their rights remain open for determination.
issues.legal_principle: The Court required a hearing for persons whose possession would be affected by implementation of the restoration order, while expressly making no determination of their rights because the record did not establish the circumstances of their possession.

predicates.restoration_order_affects_current_occupa: An order restoring premises to a former tenant would affect persons who are currently in possession of those premises.

issues.definition: If implementing a restoration order would affect current occupants, they must receive notice and a hearing before implementation.
